page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-16-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the c4d server family. It is configured with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs and 62.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes local NVMe SSD storage, providing low-latency local disk access directly attached to the host.

This server type features dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute performance without resource contention from neighboring tenants. While benchmark data is not available for this specific configuration, the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a standard general-purpose profile. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the integration of local NVMe SSD storage within a standard compute profile reduces the need for external block storage overhead for temporary data, optimizing resource density for disk-intensive operations.

The c4d-standard-16-lssd is designed for workloads requiring a balance of compute power, memory, and fast local storage. Suitable applications include relational databases, caching layers, containerized microservices, and general-purpose application servers that benefit from high-speed temporary scratch space.
